introduction.zh: 卖猫食的人捂着肚子来找杜立德医生看病，顺口给他出了个赚钱的主意：专门给动物看病。他还热情地说，自己有办法让老太太们的猫狗病得快些——只要医生点头。医生会怎么接这个话头？
introduction.en: The Cat’s-meat-Man comes with a stomach-ache and a plan. He says the Doctor knows animals better than any vet, and that plenty of old ladies would pay him well. Then he explains how he would make sure the animals get sick. What will the Doctor say to that?

sentences: 有一天，医生正坐在厨房里，跟卖猫食的人说话；那人是肚子疼，来找他看病的。

hints.zh: 卖猫食的人，走街串巷卖马肉给猫狗吃的小贩。
hints.en: The Cat’s-meat-Man: the man who sells meat for cats and dogs from door to door.

sentences: 「你干吗不干脆别当给人看病的医生，改行给动物看病呢？」卖猫食的人问。

hints.zh: 给人看病的医生；跟后面 animal-doctor（给动物看病的医生）相对。
hints.en: A doctor for people, as opposed to an animal-doctor.

sentences: 那只鹦鹉波利尼西亚正蹲在窗台上，望着外面的雨，自己哼着一支水手的歌。
她停下歌声，开始听起来。

hints.zh: 波利尼西亚，医生的鹦鹉。
hints.en: Polynesia, the Doctor’s parrot.

sentences: 「你瞧，医生，」卖猫食的人接着说，「动物的门道你全懂——比这些个兽医懂得多得多。
你写的那本书——写猫的那本，哎哟，写得太好了！
我自己不识字，也不会写——要不然，说不定我也能写几本书。
可我老婆西奥多西娅，她可是个有学问的人，真的。
她把你的书念给我听过。
哎，真是好极了——除了好极了，没别的话说——好极了。
你简直就像自己当过猫一样。
猫心里怎么想，你都知道。
还有，你听着：给动物看病能挣大钱。
你知道不知道？
你想啊，那些老太太的猫啊狗啊病了，我就把她们都打发到你这儿来。
要是它们病得不够快，我就在卖给她们的马肉里搁点东西，让它们病起来，明白吧？」

hints.zh: 这些个兽医；these here 是口语里加重语气的说法，vet 就是兽医。
hints.en: These vets: these here adds rough spoken emphasis, and vet means animal doctor.

hints.zh: 西奥多西娅，卖猫食人的妻子。
hints.en: Theodosia, the Cat’s-meat-Man’s wife.

hints.zh: 这里指识字、读过书的人，不是「学者」。
hints.en: Here it just means someone who can read and write.

hints.zh: them 的口语说法，读作 /əm/。
hints.en: ’em is a spoken form of them.

sentences: 「不行，」医生连忙说。
「你千万不能那么做。
那是不对的。」

quiz.question: Why does the Cat’s-meat-Man think the Doctor should treat animals?
options: Because the Doctor knows more about animals than the vets do.
Because the Doctor is tired of people.
Because animals pay better than people do.

feedback.zh: 他夸医生懂动物，「比这些个兽医懂得多得多」，还说他写猫的那本书好极了。
feedback.en: He says the Doctor knows all about animals, much more than the vets do.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor say about making the animals sick?
options: It must not be done, and it would not be right.
It is a clever way to find patients.
It is all right if only cats are made sick.

feedback.zh: 医生连忙说「你千万不能那么做」，还说那是不对的。
feedback.en: The Doctor answers quickly, “You mustn’t do that. That wouldn’t be right.”

grammar.excerpt: Why don’t you give up being a people’s doctor, and be an animal-doctor?

focus.zh: Why don’t you + 动词原形是在提建议，不是真问原因；give up 后面接动名词 being。
focus.en: Why don’t you …? offers advice rather than asking about a reason; give up is followed by the -ing form.

introduction.zh: 卖猫食的人走了，鹦鹉波利尼西亚从窗口飞到桌上，替医生抱不平：那些人既然不识货，不如不要再给他们看病。医生却叹口气说，兽医本来就够多了。鹦鹉歪着头，只问了他一句话。
introduction.en: The Cat’s-meat-Man has gone, and Polynesia flies from the window to the Doctor’s table. She has sharp words about people and about what he should do with them. The Doctor only sighs: there are plenty of animal-doctors already. Then the parrot asks him one question.

sentences: 「哦，我不是说真让它们病，」卖猫食的人回答。
「我指的是稍微搁一点东西，让它们蔫头蔫脑的。
不过照你说的，这么干对动物也许有点不公道。
可它们反正也会病，因为老太太们总给它们吃太多。
再说，你看，附近所有养着瘸马、弱羊羔的农场主——他们都会来找你。
就当个动物医生吧。」

hints.zh: 蔫头蔫脑的、没精神的；-like 表示「像……的样子」。
hints.en: Droopy-like: looking limp and low; -like means “in the manner of”.

hints.zh: 口语里的 isn’t／is not，很土的说话方式。
hints.en: Ain’t is a rough spoken form of isn’t here.

sentences: 卖猫食的人走了以后，鹦鹉从窗口飞到医生的桌子上，说：
「那个人有脑子。
你就该这么干。
当个动物医生吧。
别管那些蠢人了——他们连你是世上最好的医生都看不出来。
你不如去照顾动物——它们很快就会明白你的本事。
当个动物医生吧。」

hints.zh: 有头脑、明白事理。
hints.en: Has got sense: is sensible.

hints.zh: 发现、弄明白（这件事）；find out 是「查明」。
hints.en: Find it out: discover it for themselves.

sentences: 「哦，动物医生已经够多了，」约翰·杜立德说着，把花盆搬到窗台外面去淋雨。

hints.zh: 约翰·杜立德，医生的全名。
hints.en: John Dolittle, the Doctor’s full name.

sentences: 「是够多的，」波利尼西亚说。
「可他们一个顶用的也没有。
听我说，医生，我有件事告诉你。
你知道动物会说话吗？」
「我知道鹦鹉会说话，」医生说。
「哦，我们鹦鹉会说两种话——人话和鸟语，」波利尼西亚得意地说。
「我要是说『波莉想要一块饼干』，你就听得懂。
可你听听这个：卡—卡 奥伊—伊，菲—菲？」

hints.zh: 鸟语，鸟之间用的语言；后面马说的是 horse-language。
hints.en: Bird-language: the language birds use among themselves.

hints.zh: 一种薄脆饼干；「波莉想要一块饼干」是人教鹦鹉说的老句子。
hints.en: A thin dry biscuit; “Polly wants a cracker” is the classic phrase taught to parrots.

quiz.question: Why does Polynesia tell the Doctor to give up his people’s patients?
options: Because they cannot see that he is the best doctor in the world.
Because they are too poor to pay him.
Because they keep animals at home.

feedback.zh: 她说那些蠢人「连你是世上最好的医生都看不出来」，那就不值得再管他们。
feedback.en: She says they have not got brains enough to see that he is the best doctor in the world.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor answer to her advice?
options: There are plenty of animal-doctors already.
He has never thought about it before.
He would rather go on treating people.

feedback.zh: 他一边把花盆搬到窗外淋雨，一边说「动物医生已经够多了」。
feedback.en: He says there are plenty of animal-doctors already as he puts the flower-pots out in the rain.

grammar.excerpt: Give the silly people up—if they haven’t brains enough to see you’re the best doctor in the world.

focus.zh: if 从句放在祈使句后补充条件：他们要是看不出你是最好的医生，就不必管他们；从句用现在时 haven’t。
focus.en: The if-clause comes after the imperative and gives the condition; it uses the present tense, not will.

introduction.zh: 一句鸟语，杜立德医生听得目瞪口呆，急忙翻出本子和铅笔，要波利尼西亚把鸟语从头教给他——从字母表开始。到了喝茶的时候，鹦鹉却让他先看看那只刚走进来的狗。
introduction.en: One sentence of bird-language leaves the Doctor speechless. He runs for a notebook and a pencil and begs Polynesia to teach him everything, starting with the Birds’ A.B.C. By tea-time she has something else for him: a dog has just walked in, and it is talking.

sentences: 「老天爷！」医生叫了起来。
「那是什么意思？」

hints.zh: 感叹语，「老天爷」「天哪」，表示吃惊。
hints.en: Good Gracious!: an old exclamation of surprise.

sentences: 「那是说：『粥热了吗？』——用鸟语说的。」

hints.zh: 燕麦粥，英国人常吃的热早餐。
hints.en: Porridge: hot oatmeal, a common British breakfast.

sentences: 「哎呀！
真有这种事！」医生说。
「你以前从来没这么跟我说过话。」

hints.zh: 「真有这种事」，表示惊讶，不是叫对方别说。
hints.en: You don’t say so! means “Really!” — surprise, not an order to be silent.

sentences: 「那有什么用呢？」波利尼西亚说，一边掸掉左翅膀上的饼干渣。
「就算我说了，你也听不懂。」
「再给我说一些，」医生兴奋极了，冲到碗柜抽屉那儿，拿了一本屠夫的账本和一支铅笔回来。
「别说得太快——我记下来。
这很有意思——太有意思了——是全新的东西。
先给我讲鸟语的字母表——慢慢来。」

hints.zh: 屠夫记订单用的本子；医生随手拿它当纸写。
hints.en: The butcher’s order book, used here as rough paper.

hints.zh: 鸟语的字母表，指鸟语最基本的音。
hints.en: The Birds’ A.B.C.: the basic sounds of bird-language, like an alphabet.

sentences: 就这样，医生知道了动物有它们自己的语言，能互相说话。
那天下午一直下着雨，波利尼西亚就坐在厨房桌上，把一个个鸟语的词说给他记在本子上。

hints.zh: 互相、彼此。
hints.en: One another: each other.

sentences: 喝茶的时候，狗吉普走进来，鹦鹉对医生说：「你看，他在跟你说话呢。」

hints.zh: 吉普，医生的狗。
hints.en: Jip, the Doctor’s dog.

sentences: 「我看他像是在挠耳朵，」医生说。
「可动物并不总是用嘴说话，」鹦鹉提高声音说，还扬起了眉毛。
「它们用耳朵说话，用脚说话，用尾巴说话——用全身说话。
有时候它们不想出声。
你现在看见没有，他一边鼻子在抽动？」

quiz.question: What does the Doctor do when he first hears bird-language?
options: He fetches a book and a pencil and asks her to teach him slowly.
He runs out into the rain to tell the neighbours.
He asks her to say it again in people’s language.

feedback.zh: 他兴奋地冲去拿本子和铅笔，还要波利尼西亚先教他鸟语的字母表，慢慢说。
feedback.en: He rushes off for the butcher’s book and a pencil, and asks for the Birds’ A.B.C., slowly.

quiz.question: According to Polynesia, how do animals talk?
options: With their ears, feet and tails — with everything.
Only with their mouths, like people.
Only when they are alone together.

feedback.zh: 她说动物用耳朵、脚、尾巴说话——用全身；有时它们只是不想出声。
feedback.en: She says they talk with their ears, feet and tails — with everything — and sometimes keep quiet.

grammar.excerpt: So that was the way the Doctor came to know that animals had a language of their own

focus.zh: know 后面接 that 从句说明知道的内容；that 只起连接作用，从句里主语 animals、谓语 had 都在。
focus.en: Know is followed by a that-clause telling us what he knew; that only joins the two clauses.

introduction.zh: 学会动物的语言以后，杜立德医生干脆不再给人看病；上门来的换成了哈巴狗、病牛和病羊。一天，有人牵来一匹耕马，它有一肚子委屈：山那边的兽医治了它六个星期，药越吃越多，眼睛却越来越坏。
introduction.en: The Doctor gives up his people’s practice. Pugs, poodles, cows and sheep now come to his door. Then a plow-horse is led in, glad to find someone who speaks horse-language. The vet over the hill has treated it for six weeks, but what it wants is not medicine.

sentences: 「那是什么意思？」医生问。
「那是说：『你看不见雨已经停了吗？』」波利尼西亚回答。
「他是在问你一个问题。
狗想问问题的时候，几乎总是用鼻子。」
过了一阵，在鹦鹉的帮助下，医生把动物的语言学得非常好，自己能跟它们交谈，它们说什么他都听得懂。
于是他干脆不当给人看病的医生了。

hints.zh: get to do 表示「渐渐做到、终于做到」；got to learn 就是「学会了」。
hints.en: Got to learn: gradually came to learn.

hints.zh: 完全地、彻底地；gave up … altogether 就是「彻底不干了」。
hints.en: Altogether: completely.

sentences: 卖猫食的人一到处说约翰·杜立德要改行当动物医生，老太太们就开始把吃多了蛋糕的哈巴狗和卷毛狗抱来给他看；农场主也跑上好多英里，把病牛病羊带来给他瞧。

hints.zh: 哈巴狗和卷毛狗，两种常见的宠物狗。
hints.en: Pugs and poodles: two kinds of small pet dogs.

sentences: 有一天，有人给他牵来一匹耕马；这可怜的家伙发现有人会说马话，高兴极了。

hints.zh: 耕马，拉犁干农活的马。
hints.en: A plow-horse: a horse used for pulling a plow.

sentences: 「你知道，医生，」马说，「山那边那个兽医什么也不懂。
他给我治了六个星期——治的是飞节肿。
我需要的是一副眼镜。
我有一只眼睛快瞎了。
马没理由不能像人一样戴眼镜。
可山那边那个蠢货，连我的眼睛都没瞧过一眼。
他老给我吃大药丸。
我想告诉他；可他对马话一个字也听不懂。
我需要的是一副眼镜。」

hints.zh: 山那边的兽医；over the hill 就是「山那头」。
hints.en: The vet over the hill: the animal doctor on the other side of the hill.

hints.zh: 飞节肿，马腿关节的一种肿胀病。
hints.en: Spavins: a swelling of a horse’s leg joint.

hints.zh: 眼镜，比 glasses 老式的说法。
hints.en: Spectacles: an old-fashioned word for glasses.

quiz.question: What is wrong with the plow-horse?
options: It is going blind in one eye and wants glasses.
It has eaten too much cake.
Its legs are lame from pulling the plow.

feedback.zh: 马说「我有一只眼睛快瞎了」，它要的不是药，而是一副眼镜。
feedback.en: The horse says it is going blind in one eye; what it needs is spectacles.

quiz.question: What did the vet over the hill do for the horse?
options: He treated it six weeks for spavins and kept giving it big pills.
He looked at its eyes and sent it to a spectacle-maker.
He told the farmer the horse was too old to work.

feedback.zh: 兽医给它治了六个星期飞节肿，一直给它大药丸，连眼睛都没看过。
feedback.en: He treated it for six weeks for spavins and kept giving big pills, but never looked at its eyes.

grammar.excerpt: As soon as the Cat’s-meat-Man had told every one that John Dolittle was going to become an animal-doctor

focus.zh: as soon as 引出先发生的事：卖猫食的人一放出话，老太太们就上门；主句动作紧随其后。
focus.en: As soon as marks the first event; the action in the main clause follows at once.

introduction.zh: 马要一副眼镜，还指定要绿的，好在五十英亩地里耕地时挡太阳。到了门口，它又停下来，说还有件事不吐不快：谁都觉得能给动物治病，只因为动物不会抱怨。上星期就有个人试过。
introduction.en: The horse wants spectacles — green ones — to keep the sun out of his eyes while he ploughs the Fifty-Acre Field. At the door he stops with one more thing on his mind: anyone thinks he can doctor animals, just because animals do not complain. Someone tried only last week.

sentences: 「当然——当然，」医生说。
「我马上给你弄一副。」
「我想要一副跟你一样的，」马说，「不过要绿的。
我在五十英亩地里耕地的时候，它们能替我挡太阳。」

hints.zh: 五十英亩地，农场里一块田的名字。
hints.en: The Fifty-Acre Field: the name of a field on the farm.

sentences: 「当然可以，」医生说。
「一定给你绿的。」
「你知道，麻烦就在这儿，先生，」医生打开前门送耕马出去时，耕马说，「麻烦就在于，谁都以为自己能给动物治病——就因为动物不会抱怨。
其实，要做一个真正高明的动物医生，得比做一个高明的给人看病的医生聪明得多。
我那个农场主家的孩子自以为对马无所不知。
真希望你见见他——他的脸胖得好像没长眼睛——脑子跟马铃薯甲虫差不多。
上星期他还想给我贴芥末膏。」

hints.zh: 事实上、其实；用来补充或纠正前面的话。
hints.en: As a matter of fact: in fact, used to add or correct something.

hints.zh: 马铃薯甲虫，一种小害虫；说他「脑子跟它一样多」就是骂人笨。
hints.en: A potato-bug: a small beetle; “as much brain as a potato-bug” means very stupid.

hints.zh: 芥末膏，旧时敷在皮肤上发热治病的膏药。
hints.en: A mustard-plaster: an old remedy, mustard paste spread on the skin to make it hot.

sentences: 「他贴哪儿了？」医生问。
「哦，他哪儿也没贴成——没贴到我身上，」马说。
「他只是想贴。
我一脚把他踢进了鸭池。」

hints.zh: 鸭池，农场上给鸭子游水的小池塘。
hints.en: The duck-pond: the small pond where the ducks swim.

sentences: 「哎呀，哎呀！」医生说。
「我一向是个挺安静的动物，」马说，「对人很耐心——不怎么闹。
可那个兽医给我吃错药，已经够糟了。
等那个红脸笨蛋开始摆弄我，我就再也受不了了。」

hints.zh: 大惊小怪、吵闹；don’t make much fuss 就是「不怎么闹」。
hints.en: Fuss: needless noise and complaint.

hints.zh: 笨蛋、傻瓜，骂人的话。
hints.en: Booby: a stupid person — an insult.

hints.zh: 乱动、瞎摆弄别人的东西。
hints.en: Monkey with: to fiddle with something carelessly.

quiz.question: What kind of glasses does the horse ask for?
options: Green ones, like the Doctor’s.
Small round black ones.
Gold ones for Sundays.

feedback.zh: 它说要一副跟医生一样的，只不过要绿的，好在田里挡太阳。
feedback.en: It asks for a pair like the Doctor’s — only green, to keep the sun out of its eyes.

quiz.question: What did the farmer’s boy try to do to the horse?
options: Put a mustard-plaster on it.
Give it the vet’s big pills.
Sell it to the vet over the hill.

feedback.zh: 马说上星期那孩子还想给它贴芥末膏，它一脚把他踢进了鸭池。
feedback.en: The horse says the boy tried to put a mustard-plaster on it, so it kicked him into the duck-pond.

grammar.excerpt: it takes a much cleverer man to be a really good animal-doctor than it does to be a good people’s doctor.

focus.zh: much 放在比较级 cleverer 前加强语气；than 后面的 it does 代替 it takes，避免重复。
focus.en: Much strengthens the comparative cleverer; than it does stands in for than it takes.

introduction.zh: 耕马踢人的事，医生只问了一句「伤得重吗」。绿眼镜做好以后，帕德尔比一带的牲口纷纷戴上了眼镜。消息越传越远，医生家的大花园渐渐挤满了从各处赶来的动物。
introduction.en: The plow-horse gets its green spectacles, and soon farm animals all round Puddleby are wearing glasses too. The news travels from stable to field and from field to forest. The Doctor’s big garden begins to fill with animals that have walked a long way. What brings them all there?

sentences: 「你把那孩子伤得重吗？」医生问。
「哦，不重，」马说。
「我踢的地方正合适。
现在兽医正在照看他。
我的眼镜什么时候能好？」

hints.zh: 正合适的地方；马是说它踢在该踢的地方。
hints.en: The right place: the spot that deserved the kick.

sentences: 「下星期我就给你弄好，」医生说。
「星期二再来一趟——早上好！」
后来约翰·杜立德弄到一副又大又好的绿眼镜；耕马的一只眼不再瞎下去，视力跟从前一样好。
不久，帕德尔比一带的乡下就常能见到戴眼镜的农家牲口；瞎马成了闻所未闻的事。

hints.zh: 帕德尔比，医生的家乡小镇，全名「沼泽边的帕德尔比」。
hints.en: Puddleby, the Doctor’s home town, short for Puddleby-on-the-Marsh.

hints.zh: 闻所未闻的事，直译是「不为人知的东西」。
hints.en: A thing unknown: something nobody had ever heard of.

sentences: 别的动物被带来找他看病，情形也都是这样。
它们一发现他会说它们的语言，就告诉他哪儿疼、自己感觉怎样，他治起来自然就容易了。

hints.zh: 治好、治愈；不是「照顾」。
hints.en: Cure: to make a sick animal well again, not just to look after it.

sentences: 这些动物回去以后，都跟自己的兄弟姐妹和朋友说：那座大花园小房子里有一位医生，是真正的医生。
后来，只要有动物生病——不只是马、牛、狗，还有田野里所有的小东西，像禾鼠、水田鼠、獾和蝙蝠——它们马上就到他镇边的家来，于是他的大花园里几乎总挤满了想进去看病的动物。

hints.target: the little things of the fields
hints.zh: 田野里的小生灵，指各种小动物。
hints.en: The little things of the fields: all the small creatures living out in the fields.

hints.zh: 禾鼠，住在庄稼地里的小鼠。
hints.en: Harvest-mice: small mice that live in the corn.

hints.zh: 水田鼠，住在水边的小型鼠类。
hints.en: Water-voles: small rat-like animals that live by the water.

quiz.question: What does the Doctor ask about the farmer’s boy?
options: Whether the horse hurt him much.
Whether the boy had said sorry.
Whether the boy would come for treatment.

feedback.zh: 他问「你把那孩子伤得重吗」，马说踢的地方正合适，兽医正在照看他。
feedback.en: He asks, “Did you hurt the boy much?” The horse says it kicked him in the right place.

quiz.question: What happens soon after the horse gets its glasses?
options: Farm animals round Puddleby start wearing glasses.
The horse goes back to the vet over the hill.
The Doctor stops treating animals.

feedback.zh: 不久帕德尔比一带常能见到戴眼镜的农家牲口，瞎马成了闻所未闻的事。
feedback.en: Soon farm animals round Puddleby are seen wearing glasses, and a blind horse is unknown.

grammar.excerpt: they told him where the pain was and how they felt

focus.zh: tell + 人 + 疑问词从句：where the pain was 和 how they felt 都用陈述语序，不用疑问语序。
focus.en: Tell + person + wh-clause: both clauses keep statement order, not question order.

introduction.zh: 来看病的动物实在太多，医生只好请人做门：前门给马，侧门给牛，厨房门给羊，连老鼠都有了自己的小地道。几年之间，他的名字传遍各地。一天下午，窗台上的波利尼西亚忽然笑出了声。
introduction.en: So many animals come that the Doctor has special doors made: one for horses, one for sheep, and a tiny tunnel for the mice. In a few years his name is known everywhere. Then one afternoon Polynesia, sitting in the window, laughs out loud and will not say why.

sentences: 来的动物太多了，他只好请人给不同的动物做专门的门。
他在前门上方写了「马」，在侧门上方写了「牛」，在厨房门上写了「羊」。
每种动物都有各自的门——连老鼠也有了一条通到地窖的小地道，它们在那儿排着队耐心等医生过来看。
就这样，没过几年，方圆好多英里内的每一种活物都知道了约翰·杜立德医学博士。
冬天飞到别的国家去的鸟，又向异乡的动物讲起沼泽边的帕德尔比那位了不起的医生：他听得懂它们的话，能帮它们解除烦恼。
就这样，他在动物中间出了名——全世界都知道他——甚至比他在英格兰西南部人中间还有名。
他很快乐，非常喜欢自己的生活。

hints.zh: 医学博士（Doctor of Medicine）的缩写，跟在名字后表示医生资格。
hints.en: M.D., short for Doctor of Medicine, put after his name.

hints.zh: 沼泽边的帕德尔比，医生家乡的全名。
hints.en: Puddleby-on-the-Marsh: the full name of the town by the marsh.

hints.zh: 英格兰西南部，帕德尔比所在的乡间。
hints.en: The West Country: the south-west of England.

hints.zh: 就这样、用这种方式，承接上文说过的做法。
hints.en: In this way: by this means; it points back to what came before.

sentences: 一天下午，医生正忙着往一个本子里写东西，波利尼西亚照例蹲在窗台上，望着花园里被风吹得乱飞的树叶。
过了一会儿，她笑出了声。

hints.zh: 被风吹得四处打转。
hints.en: Blowing about: moving around in the wind.

hints.zh: 过了一会儿、不久；不是「现在」。
hints.en: Presently: after a short while, not “at present”.

sentences: 「怎么了，波利尼西亚？」医生从本子上抬起头问。
「我只是在想事情，」鹦鹉说，继续看着树叶。
「你在想什么？」

quiz.question: Why does the Doctor have special doors made?
options: So many animals come that each kind needs its own door.
He wants to sell the house to a farmer.
The cows have broken the old doors.

feedback.zh: 来的动物太多，他只好请人给不同的动物各做一扇门，连老鼠都有小地道。
feedback.en: So many animals come that each kind gets its own door — even the mice get a tiny tunnel.

quiz.question: How does the Doctor become known all over the world?
options: Birds flying to other countries tell the animals there about him.
He writes letters to doctors in foreign lands.
Travellers read about him in the newspapers.

feedback.zh: 冬天飞到别国的鸟，把他讲给异乡的动物听，他在动物中间就出了名。
feedback.en: The birds that fly to other countries in winter tell the animals there about him.

grammar.excerpt: he had to have special doors made for the different kinds

focus.zh: had to 是「不得不」，后面的 have special doors made 是「请人做门」：have + 宾语 + 过去分词，活儿由别人干。
focus.en: Have + object + past participle means getting something done by others: he had the doors made.

introduction.zh: 波利尼西亚坐在窗台上看落叶，越想越气：人总以为自己了不起，几千年只学会了看懂狗摇尾巴。她还说起一只会用七种腔调说「早上好」的鹦鹉。医生听着，忍不住问她到底多大年纪。
introduction.en: Polynesia has been watching the leaves and thinking about people: how pleased they are with themselves, and how little animal-language they understand. She remembers a macaw, a professor and a very old king. Then the Doctor asks her a simple question: how old is she really?

sentences: 「我在想人的事，」波利尼西亚说。
「人真让我受不了。
他们自以为多么了不起。
这世界已经运转了几千年了，是不是？
而动物语言里，人唯一学会看懂的一件事，就是狗摇尾巴是表示『我很高兴』！——这挺好笑，不是吗？
你是头一个能像我们这样说话的人。
哦，有时候人真是把我气坏了——架子摆得那么大——还说什么是『不会说话的畜生』。
不会说话！——哼！
我认得一只金刚鹦鹉，他能用七种不同的腔调说『早上好！』，一次都不用张嘴。
他会说各种语言——还会希腊语。
一个花白胡子的老教授把他买去了。
可他没留下。
他说那老头希腊语说得不对，他受不了听他把这门语言教错。
我常常想，他后来怎么样了。
那只鸟懂的地理，比人将来能懂的还多。——人啊，天哪！
我猜，要是人哪天学会飞了——像随便一只篱雀那样——那我们就别想再有清静日子了！」

hints.zh: 让我恶心、受不了；这里不是「让我生病」。
hints.en: Make me sick: here it means “annoy me”, not “make me ill”.

hints.zh: 摆架子、装样子；put on airs 就是「摆谱」。
hints.en: Put on airs: behave as if you are better than other people.

hints.zh: 哑的、不会说话的；「the dumb animals」是旧时轻视动物的说法。
hints.en: Dumb: unable to speak; “the dumb animals” was a look-down-on way of speaking.

hints.zh: 金刚鹦鹉，一种长尾的大鹦鹉。
hints.en: A macaw: a large parrot with a long tail.

hints.zh: 希腊语；英语里常拿它代表「难懂的学问」。
hints.en: Greek: the language of Greece, a byword for bookish learning.

hints.zh: 篱雀，一种极常见的小褐鸟。
hints.en: A hedge-sparrow: a very common little brown bird.

hints.target: we shall never hear the end of it
hints.zh: 我们就别想再听到别的了，意思是被他们念叨个没完。
hints.en: We shall never hear the end of it: they will talk about it forever.

sentences: 「你是一只有智慧的老鸟，」医生说。
「你到底多大了？
我知道鹦鹉和大象有时候能活得很老很老。」
「我从来拿不准自己多大岁数，」波利尼西亚说。
「不是一百八十三，就是一百八十二。
可我知道，我刚从非洲到这里来的时候，查理国王还躲在橡树上——因为我看见他了。
他看上去吓得要命。」

hints.zh: 查理国王，指查理二世；传说他战败后躲在橡树上，波利尼西亚借这事说自己年纪极大。
hints.en: King Charles: Charles II, who hid in an oak tree after a battle — her way of saying she is very old.

quiz.question: What is the one thing in animal-language that people understand?
options: That a dog wagging his tail means “I’m glad!”
That a horse’s ears show where it hurts.
That birds sing to warn of rain.

feedback.zh: 波利尼西亚说，人只学会看懂一件事：狗摇尾巴是表示「我很高兴」。
feedback.en: Polynesia says the only thing people understand is that a wagging tail means “I’m glad!”

quiz.question: Why did the macaw leave the old professor?
options: The professor did not speak Greek properly.
The professor forgot to feed him.
The professor sold him to a sailor.

feedback.zh: 金刚鹦鹉说那老头希腊语说得不对，受不了听他教错这门语言，就走了。
feedback.en: The macaw said the old man did not talk Greek right and could not stand hearing him teach it wrongly.

grammar.excerpt: The world has been going on now for thousands of years, hasn’t it?

focus.zh: 前句是肯定，附加问句就用否定 hasn’t；助动词 has 与前句一致，主语换成 it。
focus.en: The statement is positive, so the tag is negative: hasn’t it? Has matches the statement, and it replaces the subject.
